_comment: The single source of truth for every generated image asset.
Read by BOTH tool/normalise_art.py (which writes the files) and
test/platform/asset_manifest_test.dart (which checks the shipped bytes
against it). That is the whole reason this is JSON and not the manifest.yaml
the prompt pack asks for: there is no YAML parser here without adding a
dependency, and dart:convert reads JSON for free. One list, two consumers,
nothing to drift.
'tier' drives the treatment normalise_art.py applies:
1 = leakage-critical. Luminance-matched across the set and nothing else.
These are the only images an in-hand surface may show.
'face_set': the four in-match role faces. They are FOUR DISTINCT FILES, so
cross-role parity is no longer structural — it is measured, and nothing
else prevents the brightest card from lighting its holder's face more than
the others. normalise_art.py gains all four onto their common mean and
refuses to write if any lands outside +/-2%; luminance_budget_test.dart
re-measures both the shipped bytes and the rendered card. Do not widen
either tolerance to make a nice-looking card pass.
'art_only': generate_assets.py must not own this slot. The art is real and
procedural placeholder would silently replace it.
2 = gallery. Post-game only. Colour is allowed. Never referenced by a
handoff-reachable widget (handoff_purity_test.dart enforces that).
3 = public backdrop. Gained into 'lum_band' so overlaid bone-white text
keeps its contrast ratio whatever the art does.
4 = outcome plate / ornament. Post-game or on-table. Cosmetic.
'lum_band' is [min, max] mean Rec. 709 luminance out of 255.
_card_box_comment: The four paintings are finished artwork and are NEVER cropped. The painted
border, the corner letter and the corner icon are part of the picture.
That creates a geometry problem. Three sources are aspect 0.7467 and the
mafia is 0.8733, so 'uncropped' and 'identical bounds' cannot both hold for
the PAINTING. They hold for the CARD BOX: one fixed 1024x1536 rectangle for
every role, the painting scaled to fit whole inside it (BoxFit.contain, no
pixel lost) and centred, with 'card_ground' filling the remainder. Article II
is satisfied by the box — every role occupies the same rectangle, and the
golden symmetry tests are scoped to 'outside the card image bounds'.
Because coverage of the box differs per role, luminance is solved on the
COMPOSITED BOX (painting + its letterbox ground), not on the painting alone:
two paintings at identical mean brightness covering different fractions of a
fixed box still emit different amounts of light, and light on a bystander's
retina is what Article I is about. The ground is gained by the same factor as
the art so the bars never become a brighter frame around one card.
The ONLY processing applied to a face is that one scalar gain. No crop, no
desaturation, no cast stripping, no hue shift, no overlay.
_card_ground_comment: Must equal MafiaColors.dark.surfaceBase, which is AppColors.groundBase in
drift, the letterbox bars either side of a painting stop matching the screen
behind the card and become a visible frame, wider on the mafia card (76.4%
coverage) than on the other three (89.3%). That is a role tell, and no
normalise_art.py holds the bars at exactly this value and gains only the
art, so the shipped bars are this colour rather than this colour times a
per-role gain. card_ground_matches_surface_test.dart fails the build on any
drift, and probes the outer 4px ring of every shipped face.
_onboarding_comment: onboarding_* are chapter art for the onboarding deck. No source exists
yet — they are declared so the slots are named, sized and banded before
anyone has art to drop in, exactly as bg_* is. The deck renders correctly
with none of them: OnboardingCard takes a null image and prints its
chapter numeral instead, so adding one is a single line in the chapter
Card-shaped rather than screen-shaped: these appear as a band inside a
panel, not full bleed. The roles chapter has no slot — it already has the
Cold register on all of them. See HANDOFF 2a: the warm ground experiment
was reverted and is not to be reintroduced.

assets.note: What the table sees while a player holds their card. Exactly one file, shared by every role, and required to be identical turned upside down — card_back_symmetry_test.dart measures that from the shipped bytes.

Reduce Motion stand-in for bg_home_loop; the two bands must stay equal. Dimmer than the tier-3 default band on purpose - Home is the one screen whose backdrop competes with foreground art, and the four paintings have to be the brightest thing on it.
On-table phase announcement only. Never behind an in-hand turn.
The one bright surface in the app. Public by definition.
The village asleep. The card that opens the deck.
The phone going round a dark table. On-table screen, but keep it dim.
Morning in the square. Still dimmer than bg_day — this one sits inside a panel, not behind a screen.
One pair of hands holding a phone tilted away from the table.
The town at rest. The card that hands the host to a real match.
A seamless tile. Cropping or gaining it would break the tiling, so normalise_art.py refuses to touch it — tool/generate_assets.py owns this slot outright.

_emblem_comment: Listed separately because they are not photographs and are not normalised:
generate_assets.py solves each one's internal stroke weight by bisection so
all four land on the same ink coverage (27.00% +/- 0.234%) inside the same
bounding box. asset_manifest_test.dart re-measures that from the shipped
bytes. Passing them through a crop/gain stage would destroy the property.
_videos_comment: Ambient loops, shipped as ANIMATED WEBP and played by Image.asset — no
video_player dependency, no platform view. Read by tool/normalise_video.py
and test/platform/video_manifest_test.dart, same two-consumer arrangement as
ON-TABLE ONLY. A moving image is brightness that changes frame to frame, so
on an in-hand surface it breaks the +/-2% luminance budget (L-05) on nearly
every frame, and a loop at a different point in its cycle for a fast player
than a slow one is a timing channel too (L-08). There is no safe way to put
one behind a pass screen, a role reveal or a night action.
'pair': loops that answer the same question for the table (someone died /
nobody died) must run the SAME NUMBER OF FRAMES and sit in the same band. A
longer or richer animation for one outcome announces the answer before the
Reduce Motion: every loop has a still counterpart in the image list above -
takes the pair. Animated WebP has no pause API, so handing the engine a
different file is the only way to honour the setting (BRAND_KIT 9.3).

videos.note: Softened and dimmed: this is the only loop with foreground art over it. The blur is a bitrate decision (see normalise_video.py) and the band is a contrast one - the card spread is the subject of Home and the backdrop is the table it is dealt on.
